words-only.why: I compared each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions with its expect line. Check 1 tests only exit 1 and empty stdout, which is what line 1 asks. Check 2 tests for `bad config:`, the exact "$d/c.json" and line 3 / column 3. It accepts any recognisable form, so it adds no exact-wording rule. Its "different line or column is reported" FAIL just restates that the location must be 3/3. Check 3 tests only that the call throws and that the message includes the path. Check 4 tests `listening on 9000`, exit 0 and `{"port":9000}`, all from line 4. Check 5 tests that head passes and that at least one test asserting the path fails on base `src/`. The worktree steps say how to run it and add no condition. The stricter items all sit under Advisory: computing the line and column yourself instead of using Node's message, the ENOENT behaviour, and the no-defaults and no-JSON5 limits. None of them appears in a PASS or FAIL condition.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs against the repository's tracked files and package.json. All verifier commands use files that exist (`src/app.js`, `src/config.js`) and `npm test`, which maps to `node --test`. The shell syntax is valid: `mktemp`, `printf` escapes, redirects, `wc -c < $d/out`, `echo "exit $?"`. The `node --input-type=module -e` snippets are valid JavaScript and match the issue's own proofs. `git checkout <base> -- src` fits git's syntax, with the base placeholder filled in by an earlier step (finding the merge-base). The builder's formula checks out: in the four-line file, newlines sit at index 1 and 17 and 'g' is at index 20, giving line 3 and column 20−17=3, as the brief says. The builder edits only existing files (`src/config.js`, `test/config.test.js`, optionally `README.md`). The optional spawn of `node src/app.js` is also runnable. I found no invalid arguments or missing tools.

catches-traps.why:
I checked both must_catch items against the briefs, and both are handled.

Item 1: The builder brief's Limits section says word for word "Making `loadConfig` swallow parse errors or return `{}` or the defaults for a malformed file." Step 2 backs this up: "On a parse error, rethrow. Do not return a value."

Item 2: Builder step 4 says "Keep the thrown error a `SyntaxError` so the existing test `bad JSON throws` still passes." Step 1 has the builder read `test/config.test.js`, and step 6 adds tests to that same file, so the brief points to where that test lives. Step 4 does not repeat the file path, but it does name the existing test, say that it expects a SyntaxError, and warn that changing the error type would make it fail. That covers the trap.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked both briefs against the two must_not items, and neither brief does either one. Item 1: the builder brief says to wrap only `JSON.parse` in try/catch and "On a parse error, rethrow. Do not return a value." It also lists returning `{}` or defaults as a non-goal. So it never tells the builder to catch the error and return a value. Item 2: verifier Check 2 passes when line 3 and column 3 appear "in a recognisable form (e.g. `line 3 column 3`, `3:3`, `line 3, column 3`)". It fails a run only when `bad config:`, the path, line 3 or column 3 is missing, or a different location is reported. The only exact match it requires is the path string, which the expect line also requires. Wording and order are not forced into one format, so the criterion holds.

methods-private.why: The criterion holds. I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief, looking for shared PASS/FAIL conditions or probes. The builder brief has no PASS/FAIL wording. It does not include the verifier's scripts: the `wc -c` stdout check, the `node --input-type=module -e` loadConfig probe, the `git checkout <base> -- src` base-commit procedure, or the `/nonexistent.json` missing-file probe. It does repeat the expect lines word for word and tells the builder to run `npm test` and try the program by hand on c.json and ok.json. Those runs come from the expect lines and the issue's proofs, which the rule allows. The builder's tests (a)/(b) are tests it writes itself, which is also allowed. Step 3 says to "Work out line and column yourself" and gives a design check ("position is 20"). That check is not in the verifier brief, and the verifier's similar Advisory note comes from the issue's own proof 2. It is not a PASS/FAIL condition or a probe.
